ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Panama's AML/CFT statutory framework comprises: (i) Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015, as amended, which adopts preventive measures against money laundering and terrorism financing, creates the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), imposes customer due diligence, record-keeping and suspicious-transaction reporting on obliged parties including lawyers acting as resident agents and trust providers, and regulates politically exposed persons (PEPs); (ii) Ley No. 129 de 30 de octubre de 2020 and implementing Decreto Ejecutivo No. 125 de 19 de agosto de 2021, which establish the mandatory Beneficiario Final (UBO) register filed electronically with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for every Panamanian legal entity; and (iii) FATF/GAFILAT Recommendations implemented through UAF resolutions and sectoral AML rules of the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) and the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, officers, directors and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, given the US-dollar clearing environment; (ii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) the European Union consolidated financial-sanctions list; (iv) OFAC sectoral and non-SDN lists where applicable; and (v) domestic designations published by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas. Resident agents must apply FATF-compliant risk-based customer due diligence, verify source of funds, and apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval and ongoing monitoring for connected and foreign PEPs, including family members and close associates, in accordance with Ley No. 23 de 2015 and UAF regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry) — online search and name-reservation module accessible via www.registro-publico.gob.pa and the Panamá Digital citizen portal; filings are submitted electronically by licensed resident agents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be distinguishable from any name inscribed in the Registro Público and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name under Ley No. 32 de 1927 and registry norms. Names may be drafted in Spanish or in any language expressed in Latin script; a Spanish or Latin-alphabet transliteration is mandatory where the commercial name originates in non-Latin script, and the denomination must not mislead as to the entity's activities, nationality or public character. No mandatory suffix is imposed, but the name should correspond to the S.A. corporate form, such as 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.', or an equivalent clearly indicating limited liability.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Público rejects a proposed denomination, typically for identity or confusing similarity or for inclusion of a protected token, the licensed resident agent shall: (1) obtain the written denial certificate stating the legal cause; (2) correct the name and, at the applicant's option, submit a replacement name through the online reservation tool, with the first resubmission generally exempt from additional fees; (3) if the client disputes the grounds, file a written recurso de reconsideración before the Director of the Registro Público within 5 working days, followed by a recurso de apelación within 5 working days of denial of reconsideration; and (4) after exhausting administrative remedies, seek judicial review in the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. In practice, substitution of the distinctive token resolves the majority of rejections within 1 to 3 business days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The business scope is unlicensed AI video-synthesis software-as-a-service (ISIC 6201), requiring no sectoral permit or mandatory physical presence. Panamanian law permits the registered office of the S.A. to be the address of the licensed resident agent, and virtual or co-working office arrangements may lawfully be used for administrative meetings and correspondence. The mandatory statutory resident agent (agente residente) must maintain a physical office in Panama open during business hours to receive service of process; if the entity later opens a Panamanian bank account, issues local invoices or registers employees, the bank and the Dirección General de Ingresos may require demonstrable commercial substance beyond a virtual address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated below 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection for an unlicensed, low-risk software SaaS entity holding no financial, fiduciary or gaming license. The probability rises materially if the entity is controlled by a PEP, processes large cross-border flows from high-risk jurisdictions, or is selected in a UAF or SBP thematic inspection of resident agents; registered-agent premises are routinely audited, while remote entity premises are rarely inspected absent an AML/CFT trigger.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporation Law of the Republic of Panama), as amended, Articles 12, 13, 49 and 108; Executive Decree regulations on inscription with the Registro Público
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Incorporation Deed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required. The corporation may issue one or more registered, bearer, or no-par-value shares. No escrow account or bank deposit is mandated before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders accept and subscribe the initial authorized shares set forth in the Articles of Incorporation, with the paid-in capital represented by no-par-value shares and no escrow amount being required under Law 32 of 1927. RESOLVED further, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at [Registered Office Address, Republic of Panama], with [Resident Agent Name] appointed as the Resident Agent in accordance with Article 49 of the General Corporation Law. RESOLVED further, that the Board of Directors appoints [President], [Vice-President] and [Secretary] as the initial officers, confirming their full authority to open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts and conduct the Corporation's AI avatar video synthesis business with immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Nombre de Sociedades / Panamá Emprende portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online or written name search for the proposed Panamanian company name. Provide three alternate names. Upon approval the Registrar reserves the chosen name for thirty calendar days. The reservation proof accompanies the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: List of proposed corporate name alternatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on identity or similarity grounds, file a fast-track reconsideration request with the Registrar or present a revised name list without additional statutory cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Incorporation Deed Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the certified name reservation and draft articles of incorporation to the chosen Panamanian notary. The notary prepares the public deed based on the approved clauses, verifies the identity of shareholders, and obtains signatures. Deed itself is in Spanish or bilingual and must contain the registered office, resident agent, director names and capital clauses.
required_dossiers: Passport or alternate valid identification of each subscriber
Resident agent acceptance letter (if not notarized separately)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects or missing clauses, correct the deed text and execute an amendment before the same notary without proceeding to registry inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registry Filing Fees and Presentation of Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Registry Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the original notarized public deed together with the Panamanian Municipal and Ministry of Government stamp tax receipts. Pay the inscription fee at authorized bank windows or online. Request formal registration in the Mercantile Section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an observation or requisito, the corporate counsel must cure the deficiency within ten business days by filing the required explanation, corrected clause or supplemental document. Failure to cure triggers a new filing number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificado de Registro and Noticia de Registro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the inscription is perfected, request the Noticia de Registro and any certified copy of the registered public deed. The Registry issues official evidence of the corporate legal existence, registered office, paid-in capital and current officers.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney of the applicant
Registry payment receipt on the day of issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Discrepancies in the certificate may be corrected by filing a formal rectification request supported by the notarial deed; no resurrection of the company is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Initial Corporate Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office / Resident Agent of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first Board meeting at the registered office or by unanimous written consent. Approve the first board resolution, accept the registered office, register officer appointments in the corporate minute book, and open the official corporate records with the Resident Agent.
required_dossiers: Noticia de Registro or Certificado de Registro
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omission in the minute book or appointment record is cured by an additional shareholder or board resolution carrying retroactive effect as permitted under Panama corporate law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing authority applies to ISIC 6201 software activity. For the physical office, the Municipality of Panama – Dirección de Atención al Contribuyente – issues the municipal Aviso de Operación.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Commercial Activity Notice)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de la República de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – software-only virtual avatar video generation does not trigger an EIA category. Office premises with up to 100 employees and no industrial waste emissions generally qualify as minor administrative registration rather than a full EIA study.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial wastewater, VOC or particulate emissions are generated. Office sanitary wastewater must comply with Panamanian municipal sewer bylaws and Ministry of Health discharge limits; electronic waste and used lithium cells from development equipment must follow MiAMBIENTE e-waste Resolution PRD/CFM-13-2020 and the General Environmental Law Law 21 of 2021.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification must be obtained from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for the office premises, including an evacuation plan and smoke detector verification. Structural safety clearance for the building load and occupancy is required from the Municipality of Panama and, where applicable, the Ministerio de Obras Públicas. A workplace occupational hazard clearance is required from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Seguridad Social (MITRADEL) and the Caja de Seguro Social for employee insurance registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; taxpayer web portal available at https://www.dgi.gob.pa/; electronic services accessible via the DGI virtual office 'e-Tax'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) must obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) from the DGI before commencing taxable activities. The procedure for a foreign-owned entity is: (i) incorporate the S.A. via a Panamanian registered agent and register the corporation with the Sección Mercantil of the Registro Público de Panamá; (ii) file the Aviso de Operación (business operation notice) through the DGI e-Tax platform, providing proof of registered agent, corporate existence, and a Panamanian fiscal address; (iii) appoint a local legal representative or resident agent for tax domicile purposes if the directors and shareholders are non-resident; (iv) receive the provisional RUC certificate; (v) register for ITBMS as an 'agente retenedor' if applicable; and (vi) complete any complementary DGI inspection or documentary verification to obtain a definitive RUC. The RUC must be quoted on all invoices, contracts, customs declarations, and tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama operates a territorial tax system; no general check-the-box or pass-through election exists for S.A. corporations. A Panamanian entity is taxed at corporate level only on Panama-source income, while foreign-source income may be excluded by election under Article 760 of the Código Fiscal, subject to substantiation of foreign source and payment. No hybrid mismatch election is generally available. Specialized regimes permitting elective total or partial tax exemption include Law 41 of 2004 (Panama Pacifico Special Economic Zone) and Law 25 of 2010 (Headquarters Company regime), which may be applicable to qualifying AIGC exporters; these are separate administrative elections, not check-the-box classifications.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panama's value-added tax on goods transfers and services rendering, payable on most domestic and imported services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold generally exempts a business from ITBMS registration; any entrepreneur, corporation, or individual undertaking taxable operations in Panama (including digital services with local consumption nexus) must register with the DGI and obtain ITBMS tax identification from the first taxable event. However, small taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding approximately USD 36,000 may elect the Régimen Simplificado de Pequeños Contribuyentes, replacing the full ITBMS with a simplified quota or 3% tax on gross receipts where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has a mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) framework for all taxpayers. Taxpayers must issue electronic invoices using the DGI web portal or an authorized EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) software provider, and each invoice must include a digital signature (Firma Electrónica), a QR code with verification link, the seller's RUC, the ITBMS rate applicable, and a sequential number. Real-time fiscal clearance is not yet universally implemented; taxpayers transmit invoice batches to the DGI on a periodic basis (typically within 24 hours to a few days depending on taxpayer category). Some goods subject to excise taxes may require digital stamps (pólizas fiscales) or DGI pre-approval before physical movement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of tangible goods qualifies for a 0% ITBMS rate if the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory and are proven exported. Export of services, including AI video generation and software-as-a-service through cloud platforms, qualifies for 0% ITBMS if (i) the recipient is a non-resident entity or individual physically located outside Panama, (ii) the service is performed or generated for use completely outside Panama, (iii) the economic benefit occurs abroad, and (iv) the invoice is issued with the zero-rate code and accompanied by documentary evidence of the offshore nature of the transaction. Panama sources services according to the place of consumption or economic use; offshore AIGC video generation for foreign clients may be zero-rated, but services downloaded or accessed by Panamanian customers are subject to standard 7% ITBMS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SISPA electronic filing acceptance or PAN/PEDL for goods)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (for physical exports)
Commercial Invoice and export price list
Inward Remittance Certificate (from Panamanian bank) or SWIFT/transaction receipt proving foreign payment for services
Executed service contract specifying offshore recipient and place of performance
Certificate of non-residence or beneficial ownership of the client (for services)
Zero-rated ITBMS invoice with DGI QR code and export condition note
For AI software exports: ITBMS zero-rating declaration in e-invoice plus proof of offshore platform deployment or cloud jurisdiction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits export zero-rating claims retrospectively, especially for service exports and software transactions. If documentary substantiation is incomplete or the transaction is recharacterized as domestic consumption, the DGI claws back the zero-rated ITBMS input credits, assesses the 7% ITBMS with interest (legal rate), and imposes statutory penalties under the Código Fiscal (Articles 730-762). Fraudulent or benchmarked claims attract penalties ranging from 100% to 300% of the evaded tax, plus possible criminal tax sanctions and suspension of the RUC. The ordinary statute of limitations for assessment is 5 years, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud, false accounting, or non-declaration. Any zero-rating benefit improperly retained must be repaid in full before issuance of a no-due certificate, and the involvement of a registered agent does not shield the corporation from clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no statutory central bank or monetary authority. Banking supervision and AML/CFT regulation are vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) manages fiscal policy and public debt. The U.S. dollar is fully legal tender under Ley 24 de 1920 (reformed by Decreto Ley 9 de 1992), and the Republic of Panamá maintains no independent monetary issuance or foreign exchange reserve authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Currency convertibility is unrestricted because Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction and uses the U.S. dollar as domestic legal tender. Both capital account and current account transactions are freely convertible and no exchange control authorization is required for the import or export of funds. For an AI video-generation SaaS company (ISIC 6201), profit remittance and dividend distributions are treated as Panama-source income only to the extent derived from local activities under the territorial tax model; non-Panama-source revenue is outside the territorial tax base, and remittances of dividends from Panama-source profits are subject to the 5% (or 10% for certain unlicensed entities) dividend tax through tax withholding, but not to FX conversion or exchange-license hurdles. The practical impediments are compliance-driven: OFAC sanctions screening, FATCA, CRS, and SBP-mandated AML/KYC due diligence on beneficial owners and counterparties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation in Panama to surrender export proceeds to the government, deposit them in a specified bank, or convert them into local currency as Panamanian law does not maintain a central bank or an exchange-control regime. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 0%; export receipts may be retained in USD, freely remitted, reinvested, or disbursed without any timeline restriction. Receipts from the export of AI software services, subscription licenses, and virtual avatar video generation are not subject to invoicing, surrender, or repurchase requirements, although the exporter must retain standard commercial documentation (contracts, invoices, and bank SWIFT records) for tax and AML compliance purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for use of offshore digital payment institutions (e-money institutions / EMI-style processor banks) as treasury rails, but with important legal constraints. Panama does not maintain a dedicated EMI or electronic-money license under SBP law; offshore EMIs cannot independently operate a local settlement account unless they are licensed as an international banking licensee or hold an SBP-authorized payment-provider arrangement with a local tier-1 bank. For an AI video SaaS platform, a practical structure is to use a licensed Panama commercial bank as the primary USD clearing account and contract with a supervised digital payment provider (e.g., Stripe, Paddle, or Luxembourg/UK EMIs) solely for customer card-acquisition, with daily or weekly sweeps into the Panama bank account. Legal blockers include SBP AML rules under Ley 23 de 2015, the prohibition on unlicensed deposit-taking from the public, and the requirement that the final treasury settlement account reside with a licensed bank in Panama or an acceptable OFAC-compliant jurisdiction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: SBP regulations and standard Panama bank compliance practice generally require the legal representative and at least one director of a corporate client to appear physically for the account-opening interview and for notarized signing powers. Remote opening is not categorically prohibited but is permitted only at bank discretion and typically requires: (i) an apostilled and legalized corporate resolution, (ii) a notarized KYC questionnaire with wet signature or certified e-signature, (iii) a live video interview with compliance officers, (iv) certified copies of the Panama Public Registry (Registro Público) corporate registration, and (v) a valid passport and proof of address for all beneficial owners. For a Panama S.A. with non-resident directors, physical appearance is strongly advised for a high-success onboarding, while a purely remote process materially increases that bank's internal risk rating and may push the account into a restricted tier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, ADR, or PEP matching related to a shareholder, director, UBO, or customer base in the AI avatar video export pipeline.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative OFAC and EU/UN sanctions screening reports from an accredited provider for all legal persons, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners; passport copies, utility bills, and date-of-birth data; a sworn declaration explaining the business relationship and the absence of controls by sanctioned persons; a Panama Public Registry certificate showing the S.A. is in good standing; a full copy of the corporate registry / statutory registrar identifying the shareholder chain; and a contract duplicating the customer or distributor's OFAC compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substance or perceived mismatch between the company's digital AI business model and the expected revenue flows, particularly when the entity has no physical offices in Panama or has low local staffing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A detailed business plan and commercial presentation describing the AIGC video platform, target markets, retention and revenue recognition model; master subscription terms and a list of enterprise client contracts; invoices and billing records from the payment processor; audited or management accounts showing revenue from SaaS licenses and virtual avatar generation; and a Panama-economic-substance explanation documenting contracting, billing, treasury, or IP responsibilities actually performed in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership structure, bearer-share legacy concerns, or a multi-tier offshore shareholder chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized and certified share register identifying every shareholder, attached UBO declarations under Ley 23 de 2015, and a copy of the most recent annual return to the Registro Público; confirmation that all shares are registered and non-bearer; an ownership chain chart through ultimate natural persons; a certified oath by the resident agent that the UBO has been formally identified and verified; and the submission of FATCA/CRS self-certification forms (W-8BEN-E or applicable) demonstrating compliance with international information-sharing standards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume inbound remittances from numerous foreign SaaS subscribers or Paddle/Stripe payout rails creating a red flag of possible money laundering or crypto proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The payment processor's own AML and merchant underwriting package listing that the platform is a licensed or verified SaaS vendor; daily payout reports from Stripe or Paddle clearly showing the AI video-service product; a data map showing the reconciliation of individual card payments to customer contract IDs; documented refund and chargeback policies; and a transaction-monitoring SOP from the corporate treasury team evidencing that unusual transactions will be reviewed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a related entity, foreign parent corporation, or non-resident shareholder without an economic substance explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed shareholder loan or investment agreement stating the amount, currency, route, and use of funds; bank reference letters from the sending institution; source-of-funds evidence covering the investing entity's audited financial statements or tax vouchers; the group's organizational chart and any transfer-pricing documentation; and a written board resolution authorizing the capital injection and its deployment toward platform development, licensing, or working capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed as a standard international wire transfer in U.S. dollars through the global SWIFT system; no central-bank declaration or exchange-control permit is required. Appropriate MT103 field usage includes ordering customer '50K' as the positive payee company S.A., field 52 for the U.S.-dollar sender bank, and field 56/57 for the Panama beneficiary bank. The economic purpose is identified as 'Equity Contribution' or 'Capital Investment – Subscription of Shares' in the wire instruction and concurrently filed with the local bank as part of the corporate KYC file. Beneficiary bank verification requires receipt of the Panama Public Registry certificate, board resolution authorising account opening, director and UBO identification, and the source-of-funds statement from the sending investor. Compliance screening for OFAC, FATCA, and CRS must be completed, but there is no Panamanian approval timeline beyond the standard 24-72 hour bank settlement window.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound disbursements, Panama S.A. treasury functions use SWIFT MT103 in USD for recurring trade settlements, SaaS subscription payouts, and contractor payments. For high-value deliverables or enterprise sales of avatar video generation services, the standard commercial clearing rail is a documentary letter of credit opened at a Panama tier-1 bank and transmitted via SWIFT MT700/MT799 to the beneficiary's confirming bank, with invoice, bill of lading where applicable, or customer acceptance certificate. SE-credit payments are generally not used because Panama has no local clearing code except for the national low-value automated clearing house (ACH) operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá, which is reserved for domestic-only payments. For global disbursements, the reliable rails are SWIFT GPI for immediate confirmation, USD same-day Fedwire funds transfers through correspondent banks, and commercial LCs for structured order transactions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts quoted against the USD for EUR, GBP, MXN, and BRL settlement of foreign licensing fees

Cross-currency swap contracts between USD and the major foreign currencies used by customers of the AIGC video platform, entered into with a licensed Panamanian or international investment-grade counterparty
) on USD crosses to protect the translation of foreign-currency subscription receivables
USD interest-rate swaps and forward-rate agreements for managing the interest-rate exposure of treasury liquidity or term financing
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-USD LATAM currencies where deliverability is restricted or the underlying cash flows are offshore
FX spot contracts for immediate conversion when a customer makes payment in a non-USD currency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Jurada Anual de Impuesto sobre la Renta (Form 100 – annual corporate income-tax return, incl. zero return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (e-Tax 'Mi Portal')
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year S.A.: on or before March 31 annually; any DGI extension published by official notice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal-infraction fines under CTF Arts. 769–773 (US$250–US$10,000 by revenue); default interest at 1% per month on unpaid tax; failure to file permits DGI presumptive assessment and blocks issuance of 'certificado de estar al día'.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Tasa Única Anual – annual franchise fee (base bracket US$300 for paid-up capital ≤ US$10,000; US$400–US$4,000 for higher capital brackets per Law 254 of 2021)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (national e-tax system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before December 31 of the applicable calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers surcharge and default interest; RUC suspended after 60 days; certified 'está al día' clearances are denied; sustained non-payment exposes the S.A. to administrative strike-off/cancellation proceedings at the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficiario Final (Ultimate Beneficial Owner) annual confirmation and update declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos – Registro de Beneficiario Final (UBO register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconfirmation integrated with the ISR/Tasa Única compliance cycle by March 31; any share transfer or UBO change must be declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Decreto Ejecutivo 129 de 2021 up to US$50,000 per violation; RUC validity and corporate clearances are withheld until the UBO file is current.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registro Público corporate-event filings (director/officer appointments, share capital changes, articles amendments) – no annual return applies to a Panamanian S.A.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (via notarial protocolization)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of each corporate event; no statutory anniversary or annual report filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unregistered events are unenforceable against third parties; the 'certificado de personalidad jurídica' will not reflect the current board; registry fees and fines apply at protocolization.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit when gross revenue is ≥ US$3,000,000 (B/.3,000,000) in the prior fiscal year; regulated/licensed financial entities and Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV) issuers are audited regardless; the DGI may also request audited financial statements from taxpayers with gross revenue between B/.750,000 and B/.3,000,000.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá; IFRS for SMEs permitted for non-listed entities; accounts maintained in Spanish in Balboa/USD (1:1); commercial books must be legalized ('rubricado') before use.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent maintains a physical UBO file in Panama and updates the DGI register within 30 days of each share transfer or ownership change; annual confirmation is embedded in the ISR/Tasa Única cycle and is a condition for issuance of the 'RUC vigente' and 'certificado de estar al día'.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registro de Acciones / Libro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Officers (Libro de Actas y Nombramientos de la Junta Directiva)
Shareholders' Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150–US$400 per year (resident agent and registered office inclusive)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,000–US$12,000 per engagement (only triggered at the B/.3M audited-revenue threshold; a typical non-listed AI SaaS entity below the threshold does not require a statutory audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system limits Panama corporate income tax (ISR) to Panama-source income. Foreign-source subscription, licensing, and SaaS revenue is exempt from tax in Panama. No statutory tax holiday applies for general AI software activities; however, the progressive ISR schedule provides de facto relief for taxable income below B/.1.5 million: 0% on first B/.100,000, 10% on the next B/.100,000, 17.5% on the next B/.300,000, 20% on the next B/.1,000,000, and 25% above B/.1.5 million. Dividend distributions out of profits already subject to full 25% ISR carry no additional Panama tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form ISR-1 (Declaración Jurada de Renta) filed electronically via the DGI e-Tax portal (Sistema de Declaraciones en Línea de la Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, on or before 30 April of the following tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source operating revenues from AI video synthesis subscriptions, API licensing, and one-time avatar video generation output sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should instruct management to include only revenues sourced in Panama; SaaS subscriptions consumed by Panamanian customers or generated through Panamanian servers are Panama-source. Foreign end-user sales are generally outside Panama's territorial scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to Panama operations: cloud infrastructure, engineering personnel, content licensing, software development costs, marketing, and general administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain a Panama-only profit and loss ledger; costs directly related to foreign revenue are not deductible unless properly apportioned on a reasonable basis and supported by invoices and contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation and amortization of fixed assets and development intangibles, including computer equipment, interior fit-out, and internally generated software assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use straight-line rates accepted by the DGI (typically 10% for software and 20% for computers). Amortization must be evidenced by a written fixed-asset register and development cost records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or loss after applying Panama territorial source rules, limitations on non-deductible items, and all available deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Panamanian taxable result; if a loss is declared, confirm absence of Panama-source profits and document the loss for the five-year carryforward. Non-resident entities cannot claim loss carryforward without continuous filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable ISR rate schedule (0% to 25% progressive brackets; 25% on taxable income over B/.1.5 million).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the correct rate based on total Panama-source taxable income. No treaty rate reduces the Panamanian corporate income tax rate; the full 25% applies once the bracket is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed income tax payable (ISR) before credits and advance payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not subtract foreign taxes; because foreign-source income is exempt from Panama tax, no foreign tax credit is permitted. Only Panamanian provisional payments and authorized withholding credits are allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance ISR installments (anticipos), tax withheld by Panamanian payers, and any previously paid temporary taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the actual amounts paid during the year via e-Tax receipts. If none were paid, leave blank; underpayment triggers interest and surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance due or refund claim resulting from Box 6 minus Box 7.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If due, remit the balance through the DGI e-Tax portal by the statutory deadline; if overpaid, attach the tax certificate and bank account details for refund. Non-resident corporations may need a local tax ID and active bank account to receive refunds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a monthly surcharge of 10% of the tax due (capped at 50% of the tax), plus statutory interest at 10% per annum on the unpaid amount. Failure to file the annual return can result in a fine of USD 500 to USD 10,000 or more depending on the taxpayer's net worth, potential administrative suspension of the RUC (taxpayer registration), and criminal prosecution for willful tax evasion with imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid out of profits already subject to the full 25% Panama corporate income tax; 10% on dividends distributed from untaxed Panama-source or foreign-source profits (Article 733 of the Panama Fiscal Code).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction of residence, complete the Panamanian Form 3 (Informe de Pago) or the applicable withholding tax declaration, and provide a beneficial ownership statement certifying the absence of intermediate beneficial owners. The Panamanian payer submits these documents to the DGI before/at the time of payment and applies the reduced DTA rate only where an applicable treaty (e.g., Singapore, Mexico, Spain, South Korea, Netherlands) contains a reduced dividend withholding article and the beneficiary is the disclosed owner. Without a TRC, the statutory 10% withholding (or 0% for already-taxed profits) applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory Panama-source WHT of 12.5% for IP, software, and avatar technology license payments; treaty rates generally range from 5% to 10% (e.g., 5% under certain DTAs). Interest: generally 0% on cross-border loans from unrelated non-resident lenders not carrying on business in Panama; related-party interest paid for capital used in Panama may be subject to up to 12.5% statutory WHT, reduced to between 5% and 10% under an applicable DTA. Documentation showing commercial substance and arm's-length terms is required for treaty or reduced rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: PAB 250,000 (approximately USD 250,000) in aggregate related-party transactions per fiscal year triggers mandatory Local File preparation and filing of the DGI transfer pricing annex; Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated annual turnover exceeding USD 50 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2019) apply to corporations engaged in relevant activities, including AI software licensing, service centers, distribution, and IP exploitation. The AI avatar video generation S.A. must demonstrate economic substance in Panama: physical office, employees with decision-making capacity, board meetings held in Panama, and local accounting and operational records. If the entity merely licenses foreign-developed AI code and collects subscription revenue without local substance, the DGI may recharacterize it as a shell entity and subject it to 25% tax on deemed Panama-source income, fines, and potential nullification of its tax-exempt status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panama-source subscription revenue from Form ISR-1, inflating deductible expenses, or shifting profit to a captive foreign entity without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to 25% of the tax evaded plus the unpaid tax, accrued interest at 10% per annum, and criminal penalties of 2 to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to three times the evaded amount; DGI may also freeze bank accounts and reject subsequent filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Panama courts may pierce the corporate veil for fraud or evasion, imposing civil restitution on directors, travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and imprisonment for the officers who signed false returns.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a registered S.A. as a shell: no physical office, no employees, no board minutes, nominee directors, and claiming exemption for foreign-source income while carrying on AI sales without any local management or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 254 of 2019, fines of up to USD 50,000 per year per relevant activity, plus cancellation of the commercial license and reclassification of the entity's income as taxable Panama-source income at 25%; the DGI may further impose monthly defaults of USD 5,000 for missing substance records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent are jointly and severally liable for penalties and can be disqualified from acting as officers; the tax and commercial authorities may impose travel bans and personal fines on directors who knowingly operated the shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using bearer shares or undisclosed beneficial owners, or accepting SaaS subscription payments from sanctioned jurisdictions or through unvetted channels without transaction screening, in violation of Panama's AML/CFT law and the UAF beneficial ownership registry requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of USD 100,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation, mandatory reporting to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF), freezing of company bank accounts, and potential revocation of the corporate charter for serious breaches.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face criminal prosecution under Panama's AML statute, with imprisonment of 2 to 10 years, personal civil fines, and travel restrictions; bankruptcy/disqualification orders are common in serious AML violations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, service fees, or intercompany charges to a related offshore IP holding company for AI video software without a transfer pricing study, without actual functions/risks, or at non-arm's-length rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory transfer pricing adjustment to arm's-length conditions, additional tax assessed at 25% plus underpayment interest at 10% per annum, documentation penalties of USD 5,000 to USD 10,000 per unfiled requirement, and an additional penalty of up to 25% on the understatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute related-party agreements or sign the transfer pricing annex are exposed to personal liability for deliberate misstatements; criminal fraud sanctions and personal fines may be imposed when the TP arrangement is an orchestrated tax evasion scheme.
